neighbours.label: auxiliary or adverb right after the subject in a perfect/progressive verb group ('I've been', 'has long been', 'he's trying')
fire: Ever since the move, I've been unable to find a decent bakery nearby.
For almost thirty years the town has been the main supplier of slate to the region.
My neighbour says she's been meaning to fix that fence since spring.
Critics have long been suspicious of the company's accounting methods.
By the time the treaty was signed, the island had been governed by Spain for decades.
Fans are angry with the coach, and he's trying to win them back with a new lineup.
Somehow half of the committee still doesn't understand the new budget rules.
We have just finished painting the kitchen, so the house smells of varnish.
quiet: Ever since the move, I could not find a decent bakery anywhere nearby.
For almost thirty years the town supplied slate to the whole region.
My neighbour says she will fix that fence sometime next spring.

When the treaty was signed, Spain governed the island from Madrid.
